title: WPMS/2177/2020 of M/S LALLOOJI AND SONS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPMS No. 2177 of 2020
Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Rahul Consul, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. T.S. Phartiyal and Mr. Rakesh
Kunwar, Additional C.S.C. for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the parties
through video conferencing.
By means of this writ petition, petitioner
has sought following reliefs:
"I. Issue a Writ Order or Direction in the
nature of 'Certiorari' for quashing the orders
dated 4.11.2020 and 5.11.2020 passed by
the Respondents, whereby they have
illegally and arbitrarily rejected the
Technical bid of petitioner; [arising out of
Tender Ref. No. 1567/2A dated 12.10.2020
(Annexures no. 7 and 8);.
II. Issue a Writ Order or Direction in the
nature of 'Mandamus' commanding the
respondents to re-advertise the tender
notice containing true and correct
conditions so as to enable the petitioner and
other eligible contractors to participate in
the said Tender, in accordance with law.
III. Issue a Writ Order or Direction in the
nature of 'Mandamus' restraining the
respondents from finalizing of award of
Contract (AOC) in pursuance tender notice
dated 12.10.2020 (being Tender Ref. No.
1567/2A) for construction of temporary bus
stand at various locations in district
Haridwar.
IV. Issue a Writ Order or Direction in the
nature of 'Mandamus' commanding the
Respondent no. 3 to decide the Objections
of the petitioner dated 4.11.2020 and
5.11.2020 [Annexure No. 10], and till then
not to Award the Contract to any Contractor
in pursuance of the Tender Notice Ref. no.
1567/2A dated 12.10.2020;."

Case of the petitioner is that he is
registered as Group 'D' Contractor with
Uttarakhand Public Works Department. He
responded to a short term Tender notice issued
by Executive Engineer, Construction Division,
Public Works Department, Laksar, Haridwar.
His technical bid was declared to be non-responsive. Thus, feeling aggrieved by rejection
of his technical bid, petitioner has approached
this Court.
Learned Additional C.S.C. has defended
the decision taken by the respondents to reject
petitioner's technical bid. He submits that
petitioner has been registered as Group 'D'
Contractor with Provincial Division, Public
Works Department, Haridwar and, in his
registration certificate, it has been mentioned
that his registration is valid only for the Sub
Divisions under Provincial Division, Public
Works Department, Haridwar. He, therefore,
submits that from the stipulation made in the
registration certificate, it is apparent that
petitioner's registration is not valid for
participation in tender process initiated by
other Divisions of Public Works Department.
Learned Additional C.S.C. has further
placed reliance upon Government Order dated
24.08.1982. Based on the said Government
Order, learned Additional C.S.C. submits that
Contractors, who are registered in 'A' & 'B'
Category, can participate in tender process in
the entire State; while, Contractors registered
in Category 'C' can participate in tender
process within the same Circle and Contractors
registered in Category 'D' can participate within
their respective Divisions only.
This Court finds substance in the
contention raised on behalf of the respondents.
Admittedly, petitioner is registered with
Provincial Division, Public Works Department,
Haridwar, therefore, in view of paragraph no.1
of Government Order dated 24.08.1982,

petitioner is not eligible to participate in the
tender process in a different Division, namely,
Construction Division, Public Works
Department, Laksar. The said Government
Order has not been challenged by the
petitioner.
In such view of the matter, the reliefs, as
claimed in the writ petition, cannot be granted.
Accordingly, the writ petition fails and is
dismissed.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 29.12.2020
